thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — public-gateway 504 spike. Alert: ~30% of requests returning 504 from egress proxy. Root ts 2950001234. On-call: @devon

devon: Acked. Looking. Any early customer reports?

maia: Yes, multiple 3rd-party integrations reporting timeouts; support ticket 8943 shows timeouts starting ~2026-03-15T09:12Z. Impact: web UI and API calls failing for ~15% of active sessions.

sara: Seeing a pattern — subset of requests missing X-Req-ID header at proxy egress, which causes trace sampling fallback and no span. Logs show a cohort with req-id = "-".

sara: sample log:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:47Z public-gw proxy[pid=2134] "GET /v1/health" 504 - "-" req_id="-" upstream_time="12000ms"
```

tj: Recent deploy ~2h ago touched proxy header rewrite logic (PR #4821). Could be a regression in header propagation when we rewrite host headers for the new backend pool.

devon: Can we confirm whether the feature flag for header-strip was toggled? If it's the header rewrite, we should revert or toggle it off immediately.

alice: I can flip the flag and roll a tiny patch. Plan: 1) enable synthetic req-id generation at ingress (short-term), 2) toggle header-strip flag off, 3) enable verbose proxy logging to capture missing headers.

alice: Env change to enable synthetic req-id (one-liner):
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/public-gw PROXY_GEN_REQID=true
```

sara: Also turning on temporary debug logging for tracing collector so we can match traces without req-id. Will add a short runbook note for retention and disk usage.

tj: I can roll back PR #4821 -> initiating rollback to commit 7f3c2d. Starting canary (5%) now.

deploy-bot: rollback started for proxy-public-gw - canary to 7f3c2d (initiated by tj) — status: in progress

sara: Traces still sparse but after enabling PROXY_GEN_REQID I'm seeing req_id synthesized at ingress and propagated in most lines.

sara: verifying:
```
curl -v -H "X-Req-ID: test-123" https://public-gw/_health
> GET /_health
< X-Req-ID: test-123
```

maia: Customer impact note: integration A (acct 11023), integration B, and integration C reported errors. We've escalated the enterprise tickets and posted an incident note to status.redwood.com. ETA depends on rollback stability and upstream timeouts.

devon: Rollback succeeded on canary. Kicking to 100% if no regression in 3m.

deploy-bot: rollback canary -> success. Rolling to 100% (completed)

alice: After rollback, proxy logs show X-Req-ID backfilled and 504 rate dropping from ~30% -> ~2% over ~7 minutes.

sara: Traces reappearing in tracer; missing-span gap is closing. We still see a small tail of 504s due to upstream timeouts; increasing egress timeout to 35s for the heavy-payload pool.

alice: temp config patch to increase timeout:
```
upstream_timeout: 35000
# applied to pool heavy-payloads via k8s configmap
```

devon: Good. I'll hand off to @tj for overnight watch. Summary for next oncall: cause = header-rewrite regression in PR #4821; symptoms = missing X-Req-ID, trace drop, 504 spike; mitigation = rollback PR, enabled PROXY_GEN_REQID, increased egress timeout, verbose logging; customer impact = integration timeouts for A/B/C and some UI failures; status = 504s down to ~2%, traces restoring. Handoff at 09:22Z.

tj: Acked. Will keep alert sensitivity lowered and monitor dashboards (gateway-5xx, trace-drop-rate, reqid-missing-%). If we see >5% 504 again escalate to SRE pager.

devon: Thanks team. Closing incident channel once support tickets updated and postmortem draft started. :thumbsup:
